bug_semantics: SemanticsEnforcer.enforceTextSemantics sanitized text only when a semantics entry declared HTML tags. For a plain-text entry with no semantics.tags value, attacker-controlled text bypassed sanitizeHtml, then passed only length/regexp checks and was assigned unchanged to parentParams[semantics.name]. The editor filter endpoint returned that value and ContentStorer persisted it, allowing markup such as script/event-handler payloads to reach an H5P rendering context and cause stored XSS.
flaw_origin: Commit 5fd5c7b4bff58f6d3982bfd3ef2f948ed52cf540 deliberately removed the no-tags else branch from src/SemanticsEnforcer.ts, including newText = escape(unescape(newText)), and removed the tests that required script, event-handler, and SVG-style payloads in plain-text fields to be escaped. That source commit was later folded into the much larger monorepo squash 5f770a4bdfbac3d8b72bd31ca23340b9285a2d3c without changing the SemanticsEnforcer blob.

evidence: The published advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-m7gm-v253-56hh identifies @lumieducation/h5p-server, CVE-2025-47828/GHSA-m7gm-v253-56hh, affected <9.3.3, patched 9.3.3, and the omitted sanitizeHtml call; its first-party references are https://github.com/Lumieducation/H5P-Nodejs-library/pull/3894 and https://github.com/Lumieducation/H5P-Nodejs-library/compare/v9.3.2...v9.3.3. Source paths packages/h5p-server/src/H5PAjaxEndpoint.ts:617-634 and packages/h5p-server/src/ContentStorer.ts:73-85 show untrusted editor/content parameters flowing through SemanticsEnforcer and then being returned or persisted. `git log -L 235,245:src/SemanticsEnforcer.ts 5fd5c7b4bff58f6d3982bfd3ef2f948ed52cf540` identifies 5fd5c7b4bff58f6d3982bfd3ef2f948ed52cf540 as the deletion of the plain-text else branch; `git show` also shows that it deleted the plain-text XSS cases from test/SemanticsEnforcer.text.test.ts. Direct-parent verification against 124a084df16dbb4c5a68121c670eb0c21a6e7342 shows src/SemanticsEnforcer.ts still had `else { ... newText = escape(unescape(newText)); }`, so the vulnerable deletion is absent in that parent. Mainline commit 5f770a4bdfbac3d8b72bd31ca23340b9285a2d3c is a broad refactor(monorepo) squash; decomposing its preserved branch history finds the smaller source commit 5fd5c7b4bff58f6d3982bfd3ef2f948ed52cf540, and `git rev-parse` gives the identical blob b2ea1b5031e76a5554cb2b07e50e72d34fdc3ed6 for 5fd5c7b4:src/SemanticsEnforcer.ts and 5f770a4b:packages/h5p-server/src/SemanticsEnforcer.ts. Version checking finds v6.2.0 still had the escaping else branch while v7.0.0, the first tag containing the mainline squash, removed it; thus the advisory's open-ended <9.3.3 range is conservative and does not expose this temporary safe interval. v9.3.2 contains the bypass. `git diff v9.3.2 v9.3.3 -- packages/h5p-server/src/SemanticsEnforcer.ts` adds `else { newText = sanitizeHtml(newText); }`; release/backport fix e94e6e09b2a94c343893368efca27fc0c485b7db is contained by v9.3.3 and no earlier tag, while direct upstream fix d001d164eff77c11e1d686fb66831e7475f8b872 makes the same source change and is documented by https://github.com/Lumieducation/H5P-Nodejs-library/pull/3891. Finally, `git cat-file -p 5fd5c7b4bff58f6d3982bfd3ef2f948ed52cf540` supplies the exact BIC-only attribution finding recorded in ai_marker. fix_sha corrected from e94e6e09b2a94c343893368efca27fc0c485b7db to e94e6e09b2a94c343893368efca27fc0c485b7db (shipped, v9.3.3); d001d164eff77c11e1d686fb66831e7475f8b872 (direct member, not in HEAD) (reconciliation 2026-08-29: R: e94e6e09b2a94c343893368efca27fc0c485b7db ('fix(h5p-server): added sanization of text strings without formatting (#3894)') — `git show e94e6e09 -- packages/h5p-server/src/SemanticsEnforcer.ts` adds `} else { newText = sanitizeHtml(newText); }` (the exact missing no-tags branch)) fix_sha normalized to bare 40-hex e94e6e09b2a94c343893368efca27fc0c485b7db (gate format; basis unchanged, reconciliation 2026-08-29).
reasoning: Field reconciliation 2026-08-29 (see evidence tail). The vulnerable lifecycle is a regression: the earlier security implementation escaped no-tags text, but 5fd5c7b4bff58f6d3982bfd3ef2f948ed52cf540 removed that protection and its security tests under the mistaken premise that plain-text escaping was overeager. With semantics.tags absent, enforceTextSemantics thereafter left attacker input untouched before the editor response and persistence paths. The BIC is the preserved, focused source commit 5fd5c7b4 rather than the later 5f770a4b monorepo squash/move, because the former actually deletes the protection, its direct parent still contains it, and the later tree carries the identical vulnerable blob. Tag/tree comparison establishes the regression by v7.0.0, continued vulnerability in v9.3.2, and repair in v9.3.3. The release fix e94e6e09b2a94c343893368efca27fc0c485b7db and direct upstream fix d001d164eff77c11e1d686fb66831e7475f8b872 restore sanitization for the missing branch. The BIC commit object has a human author, GitHub committer, and no AI attribution marker, so the causal verdict is NOT_AI.
